scenario: A retail loyalty programme only enrolls customers who spend more than $100 in a single transaction. A marketing analyst uses the enrolled customers' average spend to project revenue from a planned promotion.

data.description: Loyalty database includes only transactions > $100. Transaction values assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $80.

question: Loyalty members average $180 per transaction. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean transaction value Î¼ across ALL customers (including non-members), and (b) the fraction of all transactions that qualify for loyalty membership.
naive_answer: The true mean transaction value is approximately $180 since that is the loyalty member average.
naive_trap: Approximately 32% of transactions are below $100 and excluded from the loyalty database. Using the loyalty average ($180) to model all customers would overstate promotion ROI by projecting high-spend behaviour across a broader base that includes many lower-spend customers.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(100-mu)/80; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+80*norm.pdf(a)/sf-180 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,100.01,179)
assert abs(mu-138.48)<2.5
assert abs(norm.sf((100-mu)/80)-0.6848)<0.01
